title: Raniag potato (NSIC Po 06): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Raniag potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Raniag potato is a potato variety from MMSU. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Raniag is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as NSIC Po 06. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 1997 Po 06. It comes from MMSU. It takes about 83 days from planting to harvest, with 17.23 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Po 06, this is the same potato. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 83 days from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 17.23 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Raniag potato takes about 83 days from planting to harvest. That is 20.5 days faster than the average of the 11 potato varieties with a day count, 103.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 17.23 t/ha trails the average of its group, 21.79. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 83 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have pale yellow flesh and brown skin. Dry matter is 18.04 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pale yellow flesh, brown skin, dry matter about 18 percent.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: mMSU potato registered for lowland growing, most preferred in Regions I and II. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Raniag potato

It suits lowland areas. Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items.q: Is NSIC Po 06 the same as Raniag?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Po 06 is another name for Raniag, registered as NSIC 1997 Po 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 83 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 17.23 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Raniag?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
